chief_complaint: heavy menstrual periods and prolonged bleeding after tooth extractions
hpi_details: 34F presenting with lifelong menorrhagia, easy bruising, normal platelet count, prolonged PTT, and low vWF antigen/ristocetin cofactor activity.
ideas: She thinks she inherited weak blood vessels and unusually heavy menstrual cycles from her mother.
concerns: She is worried that the severe bleeding means she has a uterine problem requiring a hysterectomy before she gets a chance to start a family.
expectations: She hopes for blood tests to find out why her blood does not clot properly and a treatment to make her monthly periods manageable.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Von Willebrand Disease, Type 1 evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Von Willebrand Disease, Type 1 is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes a desmopressin (DDAVP) trial and antifibrinolytics for mucosal bleeding, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: heavy menstrual periods and prolonged bleeding after tooth extractions
Key HPI features: 34F presenting with lifelong menorrhagia, easy bruising, normal platelet count, prolonged PTT, and low vWF antigen/ristocetin cofactor activity.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals normal. Scattered bruises on the shins, no active bleeding, no petechiae, no joint swelling. Bloods: Platelet count normal, PT normal, PTT mildly prolonged. vWF antigen 35% (low), Ristocetin cofactor activity 30% (low), Factor VIII mildly reduced at 42%.
Relevant background/PMH: No significant chronic medical history
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Von Willebrand Disease, Type 1.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Immune thrombocytopenic purpura (low platelet count) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Bleeding requiring transfusion — suggests a more severe subtype.
management_principles: Trial of desmopressin (DDAVP) intranasal or IV to raise vWF/Factor VIII levels for minor bleeding or before minor procedures, after confirming responsiveness
Tranexamic acid (antifibrinolytic) for menorrhagia and mucosal bleeding, alone or alongside DDAVP
vWF/Factor VIII concentrate for major bleeding, surgery, or DDAVP non-responders
Avoid NSAIDs and antiplatelet agents; hematology referral for DDAVP challenge testing and contraceptive/gynecologic co-management of menorrhagia
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 34F presenting with lifelong menorrhagia and easy bruising, plus prolonged bleeding after tooth extractions. Labs show a normal platelet count, prolonged PTT, and low vWF antigen/ristocetin cofactor activity.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals normal. Scattered bruises on the shins, no active bleeding, no petechiae, no joint swelling. Bloods: Platelet count normal, PT normal, PTT mildly prolonged. vWF antigen 35% (low), Ristocetin cofactor activity 30% (low), Factor VIII mildly reduced at 42%.
reference_soap.assessment: Von Willebrand Disease, Type 1, based on lifelong mucocutaneous bleeding with low vWF antigen and ristocetin cofactor activity, normal platelet count.
reference_soap.plan: 1. Trial of desmopressin (DDAVP) to raise vWF/Factor VIII levels for minor bleeding or before minor procedures, after confirming responsiveness. 2. Tranexamic acid for menorrhagia and mucosal bleeding. 3. Reserve vWF/Factor VIII concentrate for major bleeding, surgery, or DDAVP non-response. 4. Avoid NSAIDs and antiplatelet agents; hematology referral for DDAVP challenge testing and gynecologic co-management of menorrhagia.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical features and diagnostic criteria of Von Willebrand Disease Type 1
Formulate prioritized differential diagnosis for heavy menstrual periods and prolonged bleeding after tooth extractions
Select appropriate laboratory studies to confirm Von Willebrand Disease, including vWF antigen, ristocetin cofactor activity, and Factor VIII level
Implement evidence-based acute and long-term management strategies

teaching.one_liner: The most common inherited bleeding disorder — reduced von Willebrand factor impairs platelet adhesion, causing mucocutaneous bleeding like heavy periods and prolonged bleeding after dental work, despite a normal platelet count.
red_flags: Bleeding requiring transfusion — suggests a more severe subtype

must_ask.say: How heavy are your periods — do you need to change protection very frequently?
Have you had prolonged bleeding after dental work or surgery before?
Has this bleeding tendency been there since you were young?
Do you bruise more easily than others?
Does anyone in your family have a bleeding disorder?

history.answer: My periods have always been very heavy, and I have had bleeding that took days to stop after having teeth pulled.
My cycle comes regularly every 28 to 30 days, just as it always has.
I soak through five or six overnight pads a day on my heaviest days and regularly pass coin-sized blood clots.
My periods usually drag on for eight or nine days before completely stopping.
No, I have never missed a period or gone months without having one.
No, I don't bleed between my cycles, and I've never had bleeding after intercourse.
I sometimes feel tired or lightheaded during the heaviest flow, but I have not had shortness of breath or fainting.
I have mild lower abdominal cramping on the first day, but nothing severe or persistent.
No, I haven't noticed any acne breakout, unwanted facial hair, or abnormal body hair growth.
No, I tolerate temperature changes normally and haven't had heart palpitations or jitteriness.
No, I have not had any milky discharge from my breasts, headaches, or vision problems.
My weight has been completely steady, and I haven't had unusual stress or changes in diet.
I easily get large black-and-blue bruises on my legs from minor bumps, and when I had a wisdom tooth removed two years ago, it oozed for three days.
My gums bleed when I brush my teeth, and I used to get frequent nosebleeds when I was younger.
Yes, my periods have been unusually heavy ever since my very first cycle at age thirteen.
No, I have never needed a blood transfusion or emergency hospitalization for bleeding.
No, my joints have never swollen up or filled with blood, and they move without pain.
My mother always had awful periods and bruised easily, so I figured I just inherited weak blood vessels from her side of the family.
I'm scared there's something seriously wrong with my uterus that might lead to a hysterectomy before I can have children.
I'm hoping to get some blood work to see why I bleed so easily and get a prescription to control these heavy cycles.
I have never had high blood pressure, diabetes, thyroid disease, or any chronic illness.
I had two wisdom teeth removed two years ago, but I have never had any other operations or hospital stays.
I do not take any prescription medications, birth control pills, or blood thinners, and I avoid aspirin.
I do not have any known allergies to medications, foods, or materials.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I have a glass of wine socially once or twice a month, but never drink heavily.
I work full-time as an accountant in an office and live with my partner in an apartment.
My mother and one maternal aunt also struggled with very heavy periods, and my maternal cousin has von Willebrand disease.
I am sexually active with one male partner, and we consistently use barrier condoms for contraception.
My last menstrual period started two weeks ago, and there is no chance that I am currently pregnant.
I have never been pregnant or tried to conceive, but we may want children in a few years.
My routine Pap smear six months ago was normal, and I have no history of cervical or uterine problems.

Conjunctivae are pink without pallor; sclerae are anicteric.

Several scattered small resolving ecchymoses on bilateral shins; no petechiae, active bleeding, hirsutism, or acanthosis nigricans.
